summary_points.text: Submissions open Oct 30, 2026, 9:00 AM PT (official rules s.1; supersedes the dates page’s 1:00 PM PT); deadline Dec 4, 2026, 2:00 PM PT; prizes: Overall $30,000 / $20,000 / $10,000, category bests $5,000 ×4, Best Startup $10,000, plus bonus awards (Ghost of Kiroween Past $2,000, Best Kiro Crew App $1,000, Best Demo $1,000, and student/blog/social credit awards).
Only new projects created during the submission period are eligible; the official page instructs: do not start building your project yet.
Official themes: Resurrection, Frankenstein, Skeleton Crew, Costume Contest.
Registration requires a valid Kiro user ID or AWS account ID; Kiro sign-in is via Google / GitHub / Builder ID / organization (kiro.dev).
Owner sequencing (2026-10-26): register now; no project creation before the window opens; build after Nov 8 (D1 Nov 4 and D2 Nov 8 land first).

RULES STAMPED 2026-10-30 (official rules read firsthand): Judging = Stage 1 pass/fail (theme fit + Kiro use), then Stage 2 five equally-weighted criteria (Potential Impact / Technological Implementation / Design / Innovation-Idea / Presentation, 20% each). Deliverables: working app built with Kiro + functional app URL + text description + demo video <3 min (public YouTube) + public GitHub repo with open-source license AND a /.kiro directory at the root (specs/hooks/steering; must not be gitignored) + a Kiro-usage write-up. Skeleton Crew category: foundation plus TWO distinct applications, repo containing 2 separate app folders. Prizes: Overall $30,000/$20,000/$10,000; Category bests $5,000 x4; Best Startup $10,000; Ghost $2,000; Kiro Crew App $1,000; Best Demo $1,000; Student 1-yr Kiro Pro Max x4; Blog 2,000 Kiro credits x100; Social Blitz 3-mo Kiro Pro+ x5. Kiro credits: 4,000 one-time allotment via Credit Request Form (Kiro user ID or AWS account ID; requests by Dec 1, 12:00 PM PT).

title: Kiroween 2026 — generated concept proposal (challenge packet D4)

variants.concept: Skeleton Crew — a CMDB / reconciliation viewer run by a minimal crew: a tiny set of spec-first Kiro agents (ingest, reconcile, report) that keep a fleet inventory honest against its sources. The challenge lane's hand-noted input (input, not decision). Seeded from the repo's CMDB design (PR #1655); the Kiro project itself is created new inside the submission window.

items.item: Spec pack (inventory schema, reconciliation rules) authored in Kiro at project creation
Ingest + reconcile agents generated from specs; viewer renders conflicts with evidence stamps
Demo run against public repo data; submission by Dec 4, 2:00 PM PST

alternatives: Shrink to a single-source read-only inventory viewer if reconciliation slips; the stamped report remains the demo centerpiece.
If spec-first generation stalls, re-shell the same data model inside the frankenstein composition.
risks: Kiro spec-format learning curve inside a short post-Nov-8 window.
Reconciliation scope creep (sources x conflict types) beyond what the window fits.
Devpost deliverable requirements are unknown until the Oct 30 rules publish; the plan's demo/submission steps may need reshaping at lock.
steps: Create the Kiro project inside the submission window (on/after Fri Oct 30, 2026, 9:00 AM PT) and capture its creation timestamp into packet D4 as eligibility evidence; build work itself starts after Nov 8 per owner sequencing.
Author the spec pack in Kiro: inventory schema, source-adapter specs, reconciliation rules (from the CMDB design doc on master).
Generate the ingest and reconcile agents from the specs; keep every agent read-only.
Build the viewer: inventory list, conflict matrix, evidence-stamp detail view.
Seed the fixture inventory; run reconciliation; capture the stamped conflict report as implementation evidence (with run receipts).
Run the variant test_suites; every suite result carries its run receipt (command, exit code, output sha256, code paths).
Record the demo and file the Devpost submission by Dec 4, 2026, 2:00 PM PST.

summary_points.text: Data model and conflict matrix derive from the repo's CMDB design (PR #1655); specs written first in Kiro, agents generated from the specs.
Smallest viable scope for the post-Nov-8 build window: read-only inventory views + reconciliation report, no write actions.

Category shaping (official rules, stamped 2026-10-30): Skeleton Crew = foundation + TWO distinct applications, repo containing 2 separate app folders — the CMDB foundation carries the ingest/reconcile crew; the conflict viewer and the stamped-report app are the two applications.

test_suites: spec-pack completeness: inventory schema + reconciliation rules present and parse
reconciliation run against the seeded fixture inventory emits a stamped conflict report
read-only guard: no write/mutation action is exposed by any agent

variants.concept: Frankenstein — one new creature stitched from proven public parts: a Kiro-built decision agent assembled from the fleet's existing public patterns (Delphi Oracle deterministic receipts, the fetch_evidence provenance tool pattern from the D0 package, quota-panel display patterns), re-combined into a single new project created inside the window. Patterns are reused; no pre-built project is submitted.

items.item: Kiro project created in-window; specs describe the stitched architecture before any generation
Decision kernel + evidence-fetch tool + panel UI composed per specs; receipts on every decision
Demo + submission by Dec 4, 2:00 PM PST

alternatives: Drop the panel UI and ship kernel + evidence tool only, with the demo driven from the receipts.
Use the skeleton-crew viewer as the shell if the stitched UI lags.
risks: Translating the fleet's patterns into Kiro idioms takes longer than estimated; integration seams (receipt schema drift between components) are the likely failure point.
Three components may exceed the post-Nov-8 window at demo quality.
steps: Create the Kiro project inside the submission window and capture its creation timestamp into packet D4 as eligibility evidence; build work starts after Nov 8 per owner sequencing.
Write the stitching specs in Kiro: decision-kernel behavior (Delphi receipt pattern), the evidence-fetch contract (provenance + freshness stamps), and the panel UI surface.
Generate the components from the specs inside Kiro; patterns cross over, no pre-built code is submitted.
Integrate the components; verify a schema-valid receipt is emitted for every decision end to end.
Run the variant test_suites with run receipts on every suite result.
Record the demo and file the Devpost submission by Dec 4, 2026, 2:00 PM PST.

summary_points.text: Component patterns are all public and landed: Delphi Oracle MVP (PR #1620), D0 package with fetch_evidence (PR #1702).
Eligibility guard: the Kiro project is created in-window; only patterns/specs cross over, never a pre-existing build.

test_suites: every decision emits a schema-valid receipt (Delphi receipt pattern)
evidence fetch returns provenance + freshness stamps on every item
in-window creation guard: project creation timestamp inside the submission window

variants.concept: Resurrection — bring a dormant public spec back from the dead: pick a stalled, publicly documented fleet spec (candidates sit in the repo's ops docs and proposal registry) and rebuild it fresh as a working Kiro project, created in-window, with the original spec as the requirements baseline and a resurrection report showing what the dead version never shipped.

items.item: Corpse selection recorded with evidence refs at brief finalization (Oct 30)
Specs authored in Kiro from the original spec + gap list; build after Nov 8
Resurrection report + demo; submission by Dec 4, 2:00 PM PST

alternatives: Pick a smaller corpse at lock time; the scope cap is part of the lock decision.
If the corpse's domain overlaps the CMDB design, convert the entry to skeleton-crew and record the switch with reasons.
risks: The chosen spec's true scope exceeds the window (dead specs often died for scope reasons).
The original spec is too vague to spec from without inventing requirements.
steps: At brief lock (Oct 30), select the corpse from the repo's public ops docs / proposal registry and record the pick with evidence refs, under a scope cap sized to the build window.
Create the Kiro project inside the submission window and capture its creation timestamp into packet D4 as eligibility evidence; build work starts after Nov 8 per owner sequencing.
Author specs in Kiro from the original spec plus the gap list (what the dead version never shipped).
Build to the specs; keep a running coverage map from original requirements to implemented-or-deferred.
Write the resurrection report (coverage + gap dispositions) as part of the deliverable.
Run the variant test_suites with run receipts on every suite result.
Record the demo and file the Devpost submission by Dec 4, 2026, 2:00 PM PST.

summary_points.text: Candidate corpses are public and evidenced in-repo (ops docs + docs/proposals/registry.yaml); final pick is stamped as a packet claim at brief finalization.
Rebuild is a new in-window project; the dead artifact contributes only its spec.

test_suites: original-spec coverage: each requirement in the dead spec maps to implemented or explicitly deferred
resurrection report lists the dead version's unshipped gaps and their disposition
fresh-build provenance: project created in-window; only the spec crossed over
